tip: The -yle on aceleyle turns the noun acele (haste) into an adverb: with haste, hurriedly.
yürüyerek adds -yerek to yürü (walk) to mean 'by walking'; -erek shows the manner of an action.
doğru means 'toward' and follows a dative noun: akşam takes -a, giving akşama doğru = toward evening.
yerine = 'instead of' and needs the genitive: annem + -in gives annemin yerine = in place of my mother.
The -ken on geçerken means 'while': geç (cross) + -erken = while crossing, happening at the same time.
Arabalar is plural but the verb stays singular: bekledi, not beklediler. Non-human plural subjects take a singular verb.
unutmak takes the verbal noun in -mayı: al (take) + -mayı = almayı, so almayı unuttum = I forgot to take.
ailece adds -ce to aile (family) to mean 'as a family, all together'; -ce marks doing something collectively.
gönderir is the aorist (-ir), used for habits: with her sabah it means 'sends every morning', not right now.
gittiğimde means 'when I go': git + -tiğimde. The -diğimde ending marks 'when someone does something'.
sergileniyor is passive: sergile (exhibit) + -n- = 'is exhibited'. The -n- makes the action happen to the subject.
To want someone else to act, use -masını istemek: oyna + -masını = oynamasını, with çocukların in the genitive.
yanında (next to) needs the genitive on the noun: okul + -un = okulun yanında = next to the school.
kütüphanedeki adds -ki to the locative: kütüphanede (in the library) + -ki = 'the ones in the library'.
Here geldi (from gelmek, to come) means 'seemed': pahalı geldi = came across as expensive, not literally arrived.
varmış adds -mış for reported or inferred facts: 'there used to be, apparently'. It marks things you did not witness.
keşke pairs with the conditional -sa for a wish: olsa = 'if only there were', so keşke ... olsa = I wish.
ağaçtan uses the ablative -tan = 'from': ağaç + -tan = from the tree. It marks the source of the action.
yapabilirim shows ability with -abil: yap (do) + -abil + -irim = 'I can make'. -abil means 'be able to'.
göre (according to) follows a dative noun: anlaşma + -ya = anlaşmaya göre = according to the agreement.
almalıymış is built on -malı = must/should: al + -malı = 'should take'. -malı expresses necessity.
yüzünden = 'because of' and marks a bad cause: sıkışıklığı yüzünden = due to the jam. Use it for negative reasons.
unutmuşum uses -muş in the first person for a realization: 'I've forgotten', softer than the plain unuttum.
After a number the noun stays singular: beş ağaç = five tree(s), never beş ağaçlar. No plural suffix follows a count.
bulup uses -ip to chain two verbs sharing one subject: bul (find) + -up, then çalıştım = 'found ... and studied'.
gelen turns a verb into an adjective with -en: gel (come) + -en = 'who come', describing misafirlere (the guests).
etmişti is the pluperfect (-mişti) = 'had done': the tackle happened before he was sent off, an earlier past.
